title: Storm Floods San Francisco Streets.. and Waymo's Self-Driving Cars Stop Working! 🌧️
body: Storm Floods San Francisco Streets.. and Waymo's Self-Driving Cars Stop Working! 🌧️

Waymo suspended its self-driving taxi service in the San Francisco Bay Area yesterday, Wednesday, after several cars got stuck at flooded intersections, including the intersection of Oak and Cole and the intersection of Bayshore and Industrial. The company told riders through its app: "We have paused temporarily due to the weather," and service will return when road conditions improve and the weather clears. No injuries were recorded.

The storm that hit the area is called an "atmospheric river": about 2.28 inches of rain fell on central San Francisco by 3 p.m., breaking the daily record set in 1918 of 2.24 inches. A self-driving car relies on sensors and cameras, so floodwater on the road confuses it and it stops in place instead of risking crossing. A very important note: this suspension was Waymo's own weather decision, and it is a completely different incident from California's Department of Motor Vehicles barring Waymo cars from highways the previous day — that was a regulatory action, while this was a storm.
Would you trust a driverless car in bad weather? 🚗
